terms.definition: Deoxyribonucleic acid - the molecule that stores the instructions a living thing needs to build and run itself.
terms.function: Carries the genetic code and passes it to new cells.
terms.whereItIs: Mostly in the nucleus of cells.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the code of life.

terms.definition: The twisted ladder shape made by two winding DNA strands.
terms.function: Lets a long molecule be packed tightly and copied accurately.
terms.whereItIs: The overall shape of the DNA strand.
terms.whyItMatters: Its twist is how DNA packs a huge amount of code into a tiny space and still copies it faithfully.

terms.definition: One of the four chemical letters of DNA: A, T, G, C.
terms.function: The letters that store the code, pairing with a partner.
terms.where: As the rungs of the DNA ladder.
terms.why: The sequence of these letters is the information.

terms.definition: The sugar and phosphate chain that forms the two rails of the DNA ladder.
terms.function: Provides the strong structural frame of the strand.
terms.where: The outer edges of each strand.
terms.why: It supports and protects the code-carrying bases.
terms.whyItMatters: It supports and protects the code-carrying bases of the strand.
